summary: Modular monolith architecture: Next.js (web) + React Native with Expo (Android, iOS) with Spring Boot and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL on Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate with ALB in ap-south-1. Driven mainly by project.type and team.languages; about $2,550-7,800/month.

architecture.justification: A team of 8 benefits from clear module boundaries inside one deployable unit, without the operating cost of separate services.

alternatives.why_not: Needs 12+ people, a devops engineer, 1,000,000+ users and scalability priority 4+; here team.size is 8, scale.users_12_months is 300,000.
No workload is heavy enough to need its own service (realtime under 2,000 concurrent users, no model training, no write-heavy iot, analytics or gaming).
A team of 8 with devops=true can run long-lived servers, which cost less at steady load.

frontend.choice: Next.js (web) + React Native with Expo (Android, iOS)
frontend.justification: Next.js (web) + React Native with Expo (Android, iOS): one codebase covers both Android and iOS; suited to project.type fintech; web and mobile parts are both built on React, so component logic, state handling and the API client are written once; handles the 300,000 users expected in 12 months (about 10,000 concurrent at peak); strong security defaults for rbi_localisation, pci_dss, dpdp, iso27001. Web app: Next.js (server rendering, static generation and route handlers in one framework). Android and iOS apps: React Native with Expo (one TypeScript codebase for Android and iOS).

alternatives.why_not: Next.js (web) + React Native with Expo (Android, iOS) is preferred because web and mobile parts are both built on React, so component logic, state handling and the API client are written once.

alternatives.why_not: React Native with Expo (one codebase for web, Android and iOS): its browser build is a secondary target of a mobile toolkit, behind a web framework in routing, bundle size and accessibility.

tradeoffs: Full features are easiest on Vercel; self-hosting needs Node or a container

Enterprise standard with deep libraries for security, batch and messaging.

alternatives.why_not: Next.js route handlers scores lower on security (3.0 against 5.0, priorities.security is 5), worth 9.5 weighted points, more than its 7.2-point overall deficit (it gains some back on time to market).
NestJS scores lower on security (4.0 against 5.0, priorities.security is 5), which accounts for 4.8 of the 8.7-point gap.
Excluded: Firebase (Blaze plan) is offered by Firebase (Google Cloud), but infrastructure.cloud_preference is aws.

database.justification: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: suited to project.type fintech; a relational database suits the data: requirements.consistency is strong; strong security defaults for rbi_localisation, pci_dss, dpdp, iso27001; handles the 300,000 users expected in 12 months (about 10,000 concurrent at peak). ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Deployed in ap-south-1.

alternatives.why_not: Amazon RDS for SQL Server scores lower on cost (1.2 against 3.2, priorities.cost is 2), which accounts for 3.7 of the 4.9-point gap.
Amazon RDS for MySQL scores lower on security (4.0 against 5.0, priorities.security is 5), which accounts for 4.8 of the 10.6-point gap.

assumptions: Priced for 300,000 monthly active users (the larger of users_at_launch and users_12_months), interpolated between list-price anchors in the knowledge base.
Prices are list prices of the cheapest region inside the chosen residency zone; taxes are excluded.
Database storage is priced for 500 GB (scale.data_volume_gb_12_months).
Hosting, database and cache are multiplied by 1.5 for the 99.95% availability target (standby capacity).
The upper bound includes a x1.25 allowance for spiky traffic (not stacked on the staging allowance).
A staging environment is added for a team of 3 or more (x1.1 to x1.3 on core services).
The upper bound is limited to 3 times the lower bound: the components do not all peak in the same month, so the band stays within one order of magnitude.
A security baseline of $50-300 is added for the compliance scope (key management, firewall, audit logs).
Payment gateway fees (about 2% per transaction), one-time costs, domain names and developer seats are not infrastructure and are excluded.

basis: peak_rps: 0.2 requests per second per concurrent user, x1.5 for spiky traffic, derived
api_instances_at_peak: peak_rps / 250 requests per second per instance, rounded up
the cost band prices hosting by monthly users; per-instance sizing is added to it only when scale.peak_rps is given

warnings.message: The estimate is $2,550-7,800 a month against a budget of $6,000, so a busy month could go over.
requirements.availability is 99.95, so hosting, database and cache are priced at x1.5 for standby capacity.
The CDN (Amazon CloudFront) is used for static assets only; personal data stays at the origin in india.

ISO 27001 certifies the organisation, not the stack: the chosen services' attestations cover their part, but the team still needs its own risk register, access reviews, change records and an external audit.
CERT-In Directions (28 April 2022) require system logs to be kept for 180 days within India and cyber incidents to be reported within 6 hours; set log retention in the India region accordingly.
India DPDP Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025: Notice and consent for processing personal data; Data principal rights: access, correction, erasure, grievance redressal. The stack keeps data in ap-south-1.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022: Information security management system; Access control and logging. Managed services need attestations: iso27001, pci_dss.
PCI DSS v4.0.1: Use hosted checkout or tokenisation to keep scope near SAQ-A; Never store PAN, CVV or full track data. Managed services need attestations: iso27001, pci_dss.

RBI storage of payment system data: All payment system data stored only in systems in India (RBI circular 2018); Foreign processing allowed only if data is deleted abroad and returned to India within one business day. The stack keeps data in ap-south-1.

Make every Cashfree Payments charge and refund call idempotent (one idempotency key or order id per attempt) and store processed webhook event ids, so a retry or a repeated webhook never charges or refunds twice. Record money movements in an append-only double-entry ledger (each transfer as balanced debit and credit rows) rather than updating balances in place.
SMS to Indian numbers must go through a DLT-registered sender and templates; register before launch.
